rounds.text: SC Agrotech Ltd trades at an attractive P/E multiple of 14.9x [E1], sitting below the sector benchmark of 18.45x [E6], while also offering a favorable price-to-book ratio of 1.63x [E2] compared to its sector benchmark of 1.84x [E7]. The business demonstrates staggering fundamental momentum, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 5,684% [E17] and a compounded profit growth of 64,300% [E21], vastly outstripping sector medians of 12.6% for sales and 16.9% for profit [E71, E72]. Operating margins have expanded dramatically, surging by 118 percentage points over three years to reach 14% in the trailing twelve months [E30], supported by a conservative debt-to-equity structure of 0.08x [E38] that leaves the company almost debt-free [E57]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at ₹70 per share, offering a substantial margin of safety of 63.8% [E43, E44], with the reverse DCF revealing that the current market price implies an exceedingly modest 4.0% earnings growth against an 18.0% base-case assumption [E45]. Conceded: [E41], [E61].

The evidence reveals a stark disconnect between explosive headline revenue growth and abysmal capital efficiency, highlighted by a multi-year median return on equity of just 1% over five years and 2% over ten years [E26, E27]. This structural inability to compound shareholder capital efficiently is further underscored by a low recent ROE of 6% [E29] and a three-year low ROE of 2.62% [E60], lagging far behind the sector benchmark of 8.5% [E9]. Compounding these operational warning signs, the company generated a catastrophic negative operating cash flow of Rs -122 Cr in March 2026, leading to a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -40.67x and an operating cash flow to profit percentage of -2,574% [E34, E35, E37]. Such severe cash burn has forced borrowings upward to Rs 10 Cr [E39], while high debtors stretching to 224 days threaten liquidity [E61]. Most alarming for governance and alignment, promoter holdings have completely evaporated from 39.43% in September 2023 down to a staggering 0.00% as of June 2026 [E41]. Conceded: the company has delivered extraordinary compounded sales growth of 263% over 5 years and massive TTM profit growth, alongside a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.08x [E15, E21, E38].

Conceded: promoter holdings dropped to 0.00% as of June 2026 [E41], and operating cash flow reached Rs -122 Cr in March 2026 [E35]. However, the bear's focus on historical median ROE overlooks extraordinary recent improvements, such as TTM operating margins surging by 118 percentage points to 14% and quarterly operating margins hitting 34% in June 2026 [E30, E31]. Furthermore, the company maintains a robust, conservatively financed balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.08x, proving its financial stability despite short-term working capital swings [E38]. This fundamental operational acceleration is vastly outpacing the stock price, as seen in a 142% 5-year profit CAGR dwarfing a 17% price growth [E54]. Consequently, a reverse DCF shows that the current market price only demands a modest 4.0% earnings growth to be justified, offering a massive disconnect from actual fundamental performance [E45].

Conceded: TTM operating margins surged by 118 percentage points to 14% and quarterly operating margins hit 34% in June 2026 [E30, E31]. However, citing a reverse DCF requirement of 4.0% earnings growth [E45] ignores the catastrophic reality that operating cash flow collapsed to negative Rs -122 Cr with a cash conversion of -40.67x in March 2026 [E34, E35]. The bull's dismissal of historical low returns also fails because low profitability is structural: median ROE over 10, 5, and 3 years sits at an abysmal 2%, 1%, and 3% respectively [E26, E27, E28], dragging 3-year ROE down to 2.62% [E60]. Furthermore, pointing to a conservatively financed balance sheet [E38] completely sidesteps the alarming emergence of Rs 10 Cr in fresh borrowings up from Rs -0 Cr a year prior [E39], coupled with the total evaporation of promoter skin in the game down to 0.00% [E41]. Finally, relying on a 5-year profit CAGR [E54] obscures high debtors of 224 days [E61], an inconsistent annual and quarterly operating-margin trend [E32, E33], and a complete zero dividend payout [E59].
